messages:
Ava (sales): Customer asks for a 12mo reserved commit recommendation. Workload: embeddings daytime (~150 rps, 64 tokens), chat evenings baseline 60 rps (200 tokens) spiking to 280 rps for ~20s. SLO 250ms p95.

Rohan (solutions): Need quick calc. embeddings 150*64=9600 tps. chat baseline 60*200=12000 tps => steady ~21600 tps. Peak adds (280-60)*200=44000 => peak ~65600 tps.

Ellen (eng-infra): Conservatively assume 1400 tps/GPU for mixed quantized model => steady GPUs = ceil(21600/1400)=16. Peak transient would be ~47 GPUs but can't reserve that many.

Kai (sre): Recommend hybrid: reserve baseline for predictable load, add prewarm and burst credits for short spikes, and fallback to a smaller quantized model for extreme overload. Also set per-route token caps to avoid single long sessions blowing capacity.

Rohan (solutions): Proposed starter config for SOW: commit 12 GPUs, prewarm 4 (partial cost), burst_budget enough for +30 GPUs for 120s, autoscale max 60 GPUs, fallback route to quantized-chat when queue latency >180ms.

Ava (sales): Customer concerned about burst billing if spikes are frequent. Any wording we can give to procurement?

finance-bot: Bursts consume prepaid burst credits. If burst consumption > 25% of monthly commit capacity we will notify and recommend either a true-up or increasing the committed GPUs. Overage beyond prepaid credits billed at on-demand rates.

Ellen (eng-infra): Security note: Dedicated pools and prewarm instances are tenant-isolated; include KMS and audit log options in SOW. I'll attach sample autoscale snippet to the SOW doc.

Ava (sales): Great, I'll send SOW draft with the commit/burst language and appendix on costs. Thanks team :thumbsup:
